reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a Bitcoin-related platform or method promising 12% monthly returns and directs viewers to contact the speaker, visit a site, and obtain a Bitcoin wallet. Financial-risk disclaimers and references to Mirror Trading International videos provide context but do not remove the promotion or requested next steps.

citations.quote: If you are looking for a way to earn more bitcoin I suggest using this platform which has been at a growth rate of 12% monthly
I got a way that you can be earning it 12% monthly if you want to learn how to do that get with me it don't take much just check out the site learn how to do it get you a Bitcoin wallet.
when your money start to compound, you start understanding the power of money
the best money out here right now is Bitcoin. Believe it or not, it's better than gold. It's better than silver
If you haven't started trying to get you some bitcoin work on it work on it

opening.argument: The presentation includes an explicit limitation on the speaker's authority and a direct warning about potential loss: the screen states “Disclaimer: I'm not a financial adviser,” while another frame warns that “bitcoin can be risky don't risk what you can't afford to lose.” Those are material cautions, not language of a guaranteed or risk-free investment. The speaker also presents the subject as a personal suggestion about saving and Bitcoin, rather than certifying an outcome for every viewer. In that context, the reference to 12% monthly earnings is an opportunity to investigate, accompanied by an express warning to limit risk, not proof that viewers were promised safe returns.

citations.quote: If you haven't started trying to get you some bitcoin work on it work on it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the existence of a 12% figure and a website invitation as dispositive, but those excerpts do not establish that the speaker guaranteed the result or concealed risk. The supplied frames show the opposite: an adviser disclaimer and a warning not to risk what one cannot afford to lose. The statement about contacting him is therefore compatible with directing viewers to conduct further inquiry, not assuring them of a fixed investment return.

citations.quote: if you want to learn how to do that get with me it don't take much just check out the site learn how to do it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the concrete earnings pitch. The same speaker who says Bitcoin is “better than gold” and “better than silver” offers a way to earn “12% monthly,” then tells viewers to contact him and check the site. Saying Bitcoin is risky does not explain whether that specific platform or method is legitimate, nor does it retract the recurring-return claim.

citations.quote: I got a way that you can be earning it 12% monthly
the best money out here right now is Bitcoin. Believe it or not, it's better than gold. It's better than silver
get with me it don't take much just check out the site

opening.argument: The video's dominant presentation is informal financial education about saving, compounding, Bitcoin, gold, and silver. The speaker explains that “saving is the most important thing for your future” and discusses how money compounds, while attributing part of the comparison to a video sent by his son and mentioning Robert Kiyosaki. The frames likewise present educational topics such as “Compounding Is The Key To Financial Freedom” and direct viewers to watch videos about Mirror Trading International. That is consistent with commentary and a learning path around an investment topic. It does not show a transaction, account screen, enrollment process, or demonstrated payout, so the available evidence supports educational commentary more clearly than a proven scam mechanism.

citations.quote: saving is the most important thing for your future
Because when your money start to compound, you start understanding the power of money

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content educational does not answer its operative invitation. The prosecution's quoted language includes a specific method for earning 12% monthly, a request to get in touch, and instructions to check a site and obtain a wallet. Those are calls to take action, not merely an explanation of compounding or a neutral discussion of someone else's video. The absence of a payout screen is not evidence that the solicitation is educational.

citations.quote: I got a way that you can be earning it 12% monthly if you want to learn how to do that get with me
just check out the site learn how to do it get you a Bitcoin wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing is outweighed by the speaker's own transition from general saving advice to a concrete recurring-earnings offer. “Watch videos” and discussion of compounding do not make the promotion neutral when viewers are told that a method can earn 12% monthly and are directed to contact the speaker, visit a site, and obtain a wallet. The absence of a payout demonstration does not remove the pitch.

citations.quote: I got a way that you can be earning it 12% monthly
get with me it don't take much just check out the site learn how to do it get you a Bitcoin wallet

opening.argument: Even treating the video as promotion, the supplied material does not show the defining mechanics of an investment scam. There is no shown deposit amount, purchase requirement, guaranteed return, recruitment or downline income, fee, trading bot, pool, lending arrangement, staking arrangement, credential request, or demonstrated transfer of funds. The text only suggests using a platform, learning how to earn Bitcoin, and getting a wallet. That is compatible with ordinary promotion or referral to an external service, and the evidence does not establish that the service is unsafe. A claim that the platform has a 12% monthly growth rate is not, by itself, proof of a guaranteed personal return.

citations.quote: I suggest using this platform which has been at a growth rate of 12% monthly
get with me it don't take much just check out the site learn how to do it get you a Bitcoin wallet
start earning bitcoin daily

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution need not show every possible scam mechanic to establish a deceptive financial promotion. The description recommends a platform based on 12% monthly growth, and the speaker says viewers can earn 12% monthly and should contact him and check the site. The absence of a visible deposit or payout screen does not convert that specific earnings solicitation into ordinary commerce, especially when the requested next steps are acquiring a wallet and beginning to earn.

citations.quote: I suggest using this platform which has been at a growth rate of 12% monthly
I got a way that you can be earning it 12% monthly
get you a Bitcoin wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism is present at the level necessary for the classification: a platform is recommended, a recurring 12% monthly earning claim is made, and viewers are directed to contact the promoter, visit the site, and obtain a wallet. Whether the speaker names a deposit, fee, or downline is beside the point; the evidence shows solicitation tied to recurring financial returns, not merely a retail purchase. Calling it a referral does not establish legitimacy.
